methods.description: Move an amount from one addend to the other, keeping the sum unchanged and usually making a round number. Explain or correct a mistaken adjustment when asked.
Add the same amount to both subtraction numbers, or subtract the same amount from both. Their difference stays unchanged. Explain or correct an adjustment when asked.
Count up from the smaller number through useful whole-number jumps to the larger number; add the jump sizes to obtain their difference, including a missing digit when asked.
Split an addend into the amount needed to reach a useful ten, hundred or thousand and the rest; add those parts in order without adding the first jump twice.
Add or subtract a nearby round number, then undo the extra amount. This is an honest elementary adaptation of the explicit efficient mental subtraction scope; no filled original chain is claimed.
Find ten or a hundred more/less using the place-value change, regrouping across a boundary when needed; follow related table entries in their stated order.
